newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai July-Aug corn shortage seen at 170,000T.
newsitem.headline: Thai July-Aug corn shortage seen at 170,000T.

text.p: Thai Deputy Commerce Minister Chalermphol Sanitwongchai said on Wednesday that corn shortages between July and August could reach 170,000 tonnes.
He said insufficient rainfall will cut the country's corn output by 20 percent from its last projection.
The agriculture ministry in June put the 1997/98 (July-June) corn production forecast at 4.52 million tonnes.
Chalermphol said the current corn stock stood at 509,000 tonnes while demand exceeded 300,000 tonnes per month.
"Due to severe crop damage in certain areas, corn output this year is likely to fall by 20 percent below the projection," he told reporters.

Chalermphol confirmed that the ministry had a plan to allow the feed industry to import an additional 150,000 tonnes of corn under the tariff-free scheme to alleviate shortages but he declined to say when.
